questions.prompt: Where do gut microbes mainly reside in his GI tour?
choices: A Mostly in the acid-filled stomach.
B Primarily in the large intestine/colon—the chill habitat.
C Only on tooth enamel.
D Never in humans.
questions.explain: Large intestine/colon is where bacteria love to set up.

questions.prompt: He argues the gut is special for immunity because:
choices: A Skin is always a larger environmental interface.
B The gut is our largest interface with the environment—immune system heavily focused there.
C Immune cells ignore the gut.
D Only lungs matter.
questions.explain: Gut dwarfs skin as environmental interface; immunity surveys it.
